# Esther Chapter 4 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 457r-457v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/EST_004_page_001.jpg

---

**4:1** And Mordecai [Mordekhai] knew [yada] all that had been done [na'asah], and Mordecai tore [vayyiqra] his garments [begadav] and put on [vayyilbash] sackcloth [saq] and ashes [va'efer], and he went out [vayyetze] into the midst of the city [ha'ir] and cried out [vayyiz'aq] a great [gedolah] and bitter [umarah] cry [ze'aqah].

**4:2** And he came [vayyavo] as far as the front of the gate [sha'ar] of the king, for no one could enter [lavo] the gate of the king clothed [bilvush] in sackcloth.

**4:3** And in every province [medinah umedinah], wherever the word [devar] of the king and his decree [dato] reached [maggiya], there was great mourning [evel gadol] for the Jews [layyehudim] — fasting [vetsom] and weeping [uvkhi] and lamentation [umisped]; sackcloth [saq] and ashes [va'efer] were spread out [yutzza] for many.

**4:4** And the young women [na'arot] of Esther and her eunuchs [sarisehah] came and told [vayyaggidu] her, and the queen [hamalkah] was greatly distressed [vattitchalchal]. And she sent garments [begadim] to clothe [lehalbish] Mordecai and to remove [lehasir] his sackcloth from upon him, but he would not accept [velo qibbel].

**4:5** And Esther called [vattiqra] Hathach [Hatakh], one of the king's eunuchs whom he had set [he'emid] before her, and she commanded him [vatetzavvehu] concerning Mordecai, to know [lada'at] what this was [mah zzeh] and why this was [ve'al mah zzeh].

**4:6** And Hathach went out [vayyetze] to Mordecai, to the open square [rechov] of the city that was before the gate of the king.

**4:7** And Mordecai told him [vayyagged lo] all that had happened to him [qarahhu], and the exact amount [parashat] of the silver [hakkesef] that Haman had said he would weigh out [lishqol] upon the treasuries [ginzei] of the king for the Jews, to destroy them [le'abbedam].

**4:8** And the copy [patshegen] of the writing [ketav] of the decree [haddat] that had been given [nittan] in Susa to destroy them he gave to him, to show [lehar'ot] Esther and to tell her [ulehagid lah] and to command her [uletzavvot aleha] to go in to the king to implore his favor [lehitchannen lo] and to plead [ulevaqesh] before him [milpanav] for her people [ammah].

**4:9** And Hathach came and told [vayyagged] Esther the words [divrei] of Mordecai.

**4:10** And Esther said to Hathach and commanded him [vatetzavvehu] concerning Mordecai:

**4:11** "All the servants of the king and the people of the king's provinces know that any man or woman who goes in to the king, to the inner [happenimit] court [chatzer], who is not called [lo yiqqare] — there is one law [dat achat] for him: to be put to death [lehamit], except the one to whom the king holds out [yoshit] the golden [zahav] scepter [sharvit], and he shall live [vechayah]. And I have not been called [lo niqreti] to come in to the king these thirty [sheloshim] days."

**4:12** And they told [vayyaggidu] Mordecai the words of Esther.

**4:13** And Mordecai said to reply [lehashiv] to Esther, "Do not think [al tedammi] in your soul [benafsheikh] that you will escape [lehimmalet] in the house [beit] of the king more than all the Jews [hayyehudim].

**4:14** For if you are utterly silent [hacharesh tacharishi] at this time [ba'et hazzot], relief [revach] and deliverance [hatztzalah] will arise [ya'amod] for the Jews from another place [mimaqom acher], but you and your father's house [beit avikh] will perish [tovedu]. And who knows [umi yodea] whether for a time [et] like this [kazot] you have come [higga'at] to the kingdom [lamalkhut]?"

**4:15** And Esther said to reply to Mordecai:

**4:16** "Go [lekh], gather together [kenos] all the Jews who are found [hannimtze'im] in Susa, and fast [vetzomu] for me [alai] — do not eat [ve'al tokhlu] and do not drink [ve'al tishtu] three days [sheloshet yamim], night [lailah] and day [vayom]. I also [gam ani] and my young women [vena'arotai] will fast [atzum] likewise [ken]. And so [uvkhen] I will go in [avo] to the king, which is not according to the law [lo khaddat], and if I perish [ve'im avadeti], I perish [avadeti]."

**4:17** And Mordecai passed on [vayyya'avor] and did according to all that Esther had commanded him [tzivvetah alav].

---

## EMET's Textual Notes

1. **Mimaqom acher (4:14):** "From another place" — this is the most theologically charged phrase in the book. Without naming God, Mordecai implies that deliverance will come from a source beyond human agency. Jewish interpreters have long understood *maqom* ("place") as a veiled reference to God, since *HaMaqom* ("The Place") is a rabbinic name for the Divine. The narrator maintains the book's surface silence about God while allowing this theological undercurrent to be unmistakable.

2. **Umi yodea (4:14):** "And who knows" — this phrase expresses uncertainty, not certainty. Mordecai does not declare that Esther was placed in the kingdom for this purpose; he asks whether she was. The question form preserves the hiddenness of divine purpose that characterizes the entire book.

3. **Ve'im avadeti avadeti (4:16):** "And if I perish, I perish" — the doubled verb creates a statement of absolute resolve. The construction echoes Jacob's words in Genesis 43:14 [ka'asher shakholti shakholti], suggesting resignation combined with courage. Esther moves from passive compliance to active leadership in this moment.

*— EMET*
